messages:
maria: heads up — after the kernel 6.3.0 rollout in eu-west we started seeing a spike of pods stuck Pending on GPU nodes. scheduler logs show long wait on bind. some nvidia pods failing during NCCL init. deploy-bot: rolled kernel on 8 nodes at 03:12 UTC.

aj: saw it. also noticed an NVLINK/firmware mismatch on ~40% of hosts. dmesg shows a firmware vs driver version mismatch.

ryan: can you paste a short dmesg snippet from one of the affected nodes?

maria: paste from node gpu-eu-12:
```
[  +0.123456] nvidia: NVLINK firmware mismatch: fw=1.2 driver=1.3
[  +0.000123] nvidia 0000:3b:00.0: GPU: failed to init nvlink, nccl_init() returned -12
[  +0.000456] kworker/3: kernel:  performance counter overflow
```

olga: quick thought — if driver expects fw 1.3 but hw has 1.2 we get partial feature set; NCCL can hang when trying to use nvlink rings. we saw similar in staging last year. :frowning:

aj: short-term mitigation: cordon the oldest-firmware nodes and drain non-critical GPU pods (taint them to the old-pool). also throttle new job placements so scheduler doesn't overload remaining healthy GPUs.

maria: tried restarting device-plugin on a repro node. it re-advertised, but kubelet kept evicting GPU resources until the driver was reloaded. looks like device-plugin/device-driver handshake is fragile when nvlink init fails.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0421 — nvlink firmware/driver alignment causing NCCL init failures. Priority: P2.

ryan: longer-term options: 1) push driver build 535.86 which has a nvlink fw-tolerance patch, or 2) mass firmware update (risky, requires host reboots and vendor tooling). prefer (1) to avoid coordinated firmware flashing.

aj: agree on driver-first. question for product: will a driver that tolerates 1.2 -> 1.3 still deliver the same perf? cost tradeoffs need callout — temporary lower throughput vs large outage for firmware.

maria: scheduling/ops plan I propose:
- 11:00 UTC: cordon and set nodeSelector for low-priority jobs to cpu-only pool
- 11:15 UTC: rollout driver 535.86 via kube-daemonset, one AZ at a time, drain+reboot only if driver install requires it
- 12:30 UTC: monitor NCCL init failures, nvlink errors, and pod bind latencies
- fallback: if errors increase, rollback the daemonset and re-cordon nodes for manual remediation

aj: note on capacity — expected capacity hit ~25-35% while we rotate nodes in eu-west. estimated spot/reserve credits usage will spike; finance heads: heads-up.

oncall: approved maintenance window 11:00-13:00 UTC. keep an eye on kernel oops and GPU allocation churn. escalate if >10% of GPU pods in crashloop.

maria: I'm going to patch the daemonset manifest now to include the new driver image and add a preStop hook to gracefully drain GPUs. will post the rollout steps when ready. :thumbsup:

ryan: also adding a temporary alert: HighGPUAllocationBindLatency (>90s) -> page oncall.

maria: copying checklist below for the rollout (keeping it small):
1) cordon old-fw nodes: `kubectl cordon gpu-eu-*old*`
2) drain non-critical stacks: `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`
3) patch daemonset image -> `redwood/driver:535.86-tol1`
4) roll by AZ with `kubectl rollout restart ds/gpu-driver -n kube-system`
5) watch `kubectl get pods -n ml -o wide` and `kubectl logs ds/gpu-device-plugin -n kube-system`

aj: sounds good. keep this channel updated with time and any failed nodes.

maria: will do, posting progress logs under INC-2026-0421. tagging @oncall for immediate paging if NCCL errors spike.

oncall: acknowledged. I'll be live on the channel during the window.

maria: thanks — starting prechecks now. will update after the first AZ rollout.
